$comment: Lines that may legitimately name the parent tool. Every other occurrence of
rosync / ro-sync / 'ro sync' / 7878 in docs/, src/, plugin/src/, desktop/src/,
README.md, NOTICE or CHANGELOG.md fails check-heritage.mjs.
An entry allows a hit only when the file path, the token id AND the exact
`contains` text all match, up to `max` lines. Blanket file exemptions are
deliberately impossible: an allowlisted file must still not leak the name
anywhere except the sentence that earned the exemption.
Adding an entry means asserting that the string is attribution or design
rationale, not a leftover. If it is a leftover, fix the source instead.

allow.reason: Provenance statement. NOTICE records what WSync is derived from and what it is not: the engine is an Apache-2.0 fork of Argon (attribution legally required), the product layer is a remake of the author's own prior tool (stated so the Argon attribution is not read as covering the whole product). Naming the parent is the entire point of the file.
The README's Attribution section mirrors NOTICE for readers who never open it. Same justification: it points at the licence obligation for Argon and disclaims that obligation for the product layer.

Opening one-line description of what WSync is (Design 1.3, heritage map). The project is defined by combining two lineages, and the first sentence has to say which two; the alternative is a README that describes the tool inaccurately to protect a naming rule.

Design-rationale comment: it records that the reference implementation had a fifth `host` theme preset for its terminal-widget surface and that WSync deliberately ships four, because WSync has only the desktop window (Design 1.4). Without the reference the omission reads like an oversight and someone re-adds it. Comment only, never rendered.

Provenance note on a wire contract: the seven remote-op error codes (Design 5.3) are carried over unchanged, and the comment says so. A maintainer who does not know the codes are a compatibility surface will eventually rename one. Comment only; the codes themselves carry no heritage naming.

Records where a deliberate v1 semantic restriction comes from: selector segments have no partial-segment globs, so `Work*` is a literal name. Stating the source is what stops someone 'fixing' it into a glob and silently changing query semantics.

Cites the origin of a connection-lifecycle invariant (every connect has a deadline). Design 15 phase 7 names Ro-Sync's invariant list as the seed for WSync's own, so an inline citation is the intended form until that document exists. Doc comment on a constant; the constant and its value are WSync's.

Cites the origin of the codec budget limits (depth 64 / 20000 nodes / 10000 entries / 4 MiB strings). They are a carried-over wire contract (Design 5.4); the citation is what stops someone rounding them to nicer numbers. Comment only.
Records the reference semantics for mixed/array table encoding, a wire-compatibility behavior the CLI depends on. Comment only.
Records that canonical string forms for non-finite numbers follow the reference implementation. Comment only.

The get/props full-view shape (properties/attributes/tags/children, Ref and SharedString omitted) is a registry contract carried from the reference; the comment marks output-shape parity as deliberate. Comment only.

Same justification as the existing Remote/Error.luau entry: the seven wire error codes are a compatibility surface kept verbatim (Design 5.3/5.4), and the dispatch layer restates it where the codes are consumed. Comment only.

Module doc for the daemon lifecycle (records, locks, boot-guarded stop): Design 3.2/11/12 define this subsystem as the Ro-Sync model rebuilt clean-room, and the module header says exactly that. Internal doc comment, never user-visible.

Cites the origin of the watchdog's 5-minute + 30-second suspect-grace shape. The grace window looks redundant until you know it exists for laptop sleep; the citation prevents its removal. Internal doc comment.
Daemon-side twin of the plugin's error-code provenance notes: the same seven wire codes, same carried-over contract, cited where the Rust enum defines them. Internal doc comment.

Module doc for the conflict engine: Design 6.3 defines it as Ro-Sync's per-path baseline engine generalized to instances, and the header says exactly that, including where the fail-closed race-window stance comes from. Internal doc comment.

Design rationale: records that the reference implementation lazy-loaded its diff library from a public CDN (a documented Design 8.2 fix — 'no CDN dependency') and why this module is dependency-free instead. The citation is what stops someone 'simplifying' back to a CDN import. Comment only.

Provenance of the new-instance apply order (props while unparented, parent late, Source after parenting) — an ordering that exists because UpdateSourceAsync requires a rooted script. Naming the source marks it deliberate. Comment only.

allow.contains: exactly like Ro-Sync: a dropped marker costs undo labelling
allow.reason: Provenance of the single-write --waypoint semantics: the pre-write marker is best-effort (warn on failure, never block the write) because the plugin auto-seals every mutation — the reference established that failure mode split. Comment only.

Provenance of the capture technique (CaptureService screenshot -> EditableImage readback with dual-pass alpha recovery) — the reference proved this API path works without screenshot permissions; the citation stops someone swapping it for a permission-gated approach. Comment only.

Module doc citing the section arc the generated agent docs follow (Design 10.6 mandates mirroring ro-sync.md 0-7). The generated OUTPUT no longer names Ro-Sync anywhere; only this internal doc comment records the structural source.

allow.contains: the same way Ro-Sync's workflow engine was
allow.reason: Module doc citing the structural source of the workflow engine split (typed schema / whole-plan validator / executor) — run.json's schema-v1 contract is carried over, and the comment records where the shape that satisfies it came from. Internal doc comment.

Provenance of the connection-direction-first DataModel detection order — the one that survives Run mode's misleading HostDataModelType. Citing the source stops a 'simplification' back to the naive order that misclassifies Run mode. Comment only.
Signal-coordination bounds carried from the reference implementation's tested values (queue depths, backlog caps). Comment only.
Header citing the user ruling that the connection card follows the Ro-Sync model (portless auto-discovery, two-step create). Comment only.
Same ruling citation on the pure policy module (strict GameId matching, state machine). Comment only.
Same ruling citation on the scan orchestrator. Comment only.
